NTSB-JT610-STYLE-001: Paraphrased scenario consistent with public Lion Air Flight 610 findings: erroneous angle of attack (AoA) data led to activation of the Maneuvering Characteristics Augmentation System (MCAS), which repeatedly commanded nose-down stabilizer trim. Flight crew experienced difficulty maintaining altitude; unreliable airspeed and disagree alerts complicated diagnosis. The sequence illustrates automation surprise tied to single AoA input and trim authority.
NTSB-ET302-STYLE-001: Paraphrased scenario consistent with public Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302 findings: shortly after takeoff, MCAS activated in response to erroneous AoA; crew used manual electric trim and cutout; difficulty recovering full trim authority and high workload contributed to loss of control. Training and checklist familiarity with runaway trim and MCAS recovery are central themes.
NTSB-737-TRIM-STYLE: Uncommanded stabilizer motion consistent with trim runaway scenarios: nose-down trim commands continued despite crew inputs; manual electric trim and stabilizer trim cutout are primary mitigations; crew must maintain aircraft control while diagnosing flight control anomalies.
